clue.text: The solitary person looking for Nehru on telly?

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone alone in front of the television, scanning the channels for the Indian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram indicator word: the question mark asks you to rearrange Nehru on telly into LONELY HUNTER, half of the McCullers title The Heart is a Lonely Hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary gives the adjective lonely, and someone out searching or tracking is a hunter.

clue.text: Halt, friend, at stile?

blocks.note: halt is an old adjective for limping or crippled
the dog is man's best friend

explanation.surface: A sentry's challenge, 'Halt, friend!', shouted at someone climbing a stile.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also points to the saying about helping a lame dog over a stile, meaning assisting someone in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A crippled animal waiting at a stile is the proverbial figure needing a helping hand to get over.

clue.text: Nearly (almost) half a dozen coming in with apprehension

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so one letter is dropped
something coming in enters the middle of the other word and sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, before losing its A

explanation.surface: Six people arrive almost together, nervous about what awaits them.
explanation.walkthrough: Nearly loses its A to become NERLY, and the Roman six goes inside it after NER.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something nervily means acting anxiously, full of fear and nervous tension.

clue.text: Pub now closing? Depends on the meridian

definitions.note: a description of the noun phrase rather than a synonym

blocks.note: your local is the nearby pub you usually visit
'Time, gentlemen, please' is the landlord's call at closing

explanation.surface: Asking whether the pub is shutting now, with the answer that it varies by longitude.
explanation.walkthrough: British pubs call 'time' at closing; a local is your regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock time in a given place is set by its longitude relative to Greenwich, so it varies with the meridian.

clue.text: 16's was 1 across, having skill with explosive

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle about a writer's novel, plus a talent with bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: McCullers's novel is The Heart is a Lonely Hunter, so her heart was a lonely hunter; 'with' places the explosive alongside the skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the McCullers novel states that the organ of feeling is a lonely hunter.

clue.text: Agreement about prison? Nothing is impossible

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the second

explanation.surface: A deal about a jail sentence turns out to be unworkable.
explanation.definitionFit: The pidgin phrase is a flat refusal, said of something that cannot be done at all.

clue.text: Contributor to the Listener committing a murder

indicators.note: committing a crime suggests mayhem, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A writer for The Listener magazine turns out to be a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC weekly magazine; here the listener is simply anyone hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear vibrates with sound, so it plays a part in anyone's hearing.

clue.text: No feast for Clare at the house?

blocks.note: the House of Commons, where MPs sit

explanation.surface: A meagre meal laid on for someone named Clare at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a Labour MP and cabinet minister, so she sat in the Commons; 'Clare' looks like the Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scant rations, a meagre allowance of food rather than plenty.

clue.text: The Odyssey is its destination with king in charge

definitions.note: a description: the answer is the adjective the Odyssey belongs under

blocks.note: home is where a journey ends

explanation.surface: Odysseus's epic voyage ends at home, where he returns as king to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the story itself: Odysseus's goal was his home in Ithaca, where he was king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odyssey is attributed to the poet Homer, so it is a Homeric epic by authorship.

clue.text: Much of the weed on roads is in harmony

indicators.note: much of means a large part but not all, so some letters are dropped

blocks.note: the weed is a nickname for tobacco

explanation.surface: Weeds growing over the roads seem to sit in harmony with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the back four letters of tobacco are kept, a generous use of 'much of'. In an across clue, 'on' puts the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord with something is to agree or match it, so the verb means being in agreement.

clue.text: Listen, maybe, before you leap to 26's work

indicators.note: maybe hints that the word is a possible rearrangement of another, not itself

blocks.note: taken as written, then its six letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to pay attention before jumping, like 'look before you leap'.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring (1962), the book that launched the modern environmental movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1962 book on pesticides is the best-known title by the American biologist at 26.

clue.text: Left father or son driving in Surrey

definitions.note: a location, standing for a town in that county

blocks.note: red is the colour of the political left
Graham Hill and his son Damon were both Formula One world champions

explanation.surface: A man left behind a father or son who was driving through Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south of London; Redhill is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Redhill is a town in the English county, so the place is found within it.

clue.text: Nurse at stream said to want climbing aid

indicators.note: said means we go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: to tend is to nurse or look after
a rill is a small brook

explanation.surface: A nurse standing by a brook wishes for something to help her climb.
explanation.walkthrough: Tend rill spoken runs together as the answer, with a single L.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant uses thin coiling shoots to grip supports as it grows upward.

clue.text: Imprison youth leader for being cautious

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to cage is to lock up

explanation.surface: Lock up the head of a youth gang for being careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guarded and reluctant to give information away is described as wary and secretive.

clue.text: Is young Blair a supporter? Insert number in Irish Sea

definitions.note: a location, standing for the island found there

indicators.note: insert tells us to put one thing inside another

blocks.note: Leo Blair, the son born to Tony and Cherie Blair at Downing Street in 2000
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Tony Blair's baby son backs a team, then a stray instruction about the Irish Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The number goes inside FAN after its F.
explanation.definitionFit: The self-governing Crown dependency is an island sitting between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Girl heard by another in Portugal, maybe

indicators.note: heard means we take the girl's name by its sound

explanation.surface: One girl overheard by another while on holiday in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusitania was the Roman province roughly covering modern Portugal, hence 'maybe' for an approximate match.

clue.text: 26 part 2 is the name for those who select and destroy soldier's ...

definitions.note: the novelist whose first name is the surname of 26

blocks.note: the dots run on to 19, so the soldier's cross is the Military Cross
culling is selective killing of animals

explanation.surface: A sentence about pest controllers that trails off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Carson McCullers's first name matches Rachel Carson's surname. The dots continue the clue into 19 across, so 'soldier's cross' is MC.
explanation.definitionFit: Carson McCullers, the Southern novelist, has as forename the second half of the writer at 26.

clue.text: A pair of aces, possibly, held model in Wales, you may say

definitions.note: sounds like whales, the animals the order contains

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could take a different arrangement
held means kept inside, so one piece sits within the other

explanation.surface: A gambler's two aces and a fashion model turn up in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Wales said aloud is 'whales', and the answer is the zoological order of whales and dolphins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetacea is the scientific order of marine mammals including whales, dolphins and porpoises.

clue.text: Archiepiscopal spot of honour in a strip

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A place where an archbishop receives an honour in a narrow strip of land.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth Palace in London is the official residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district holds the palace where the Archbishop of Canterbury lives, so it is his seat.

clue.text: ... sign of ill temper

blocks.note: first meaning: a mark such as X or a crucifix

explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry 16's 'soldier's' into this clue, so 'soldier's cross' gives MC there while this light stands as a double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a shape of two crossing lines and also means irritated or angry.

clue.text: Trick: swear to damage the brain

explanation.surface: Fooling someone and cursing at them leads to a head injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow to the head that jolts and injures the brain is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Greek character of moronic disposition

indicators.note: disposition can mean arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A person in Greece with a stupid temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person and 'disposition' a temperament, but character is a letter and disposition an arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, short o.

clue.text: The best possible plot with aim revealed

indicators.note: revealed suggests the true form hidden in these letters is laid bare by rearranging

explanation.surface: A conspiracy whose purpose has come to light is the ideal outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal describes the most favourable or ideal outcome among the alternatives available.

clue.text: True ally worried about love

indicators.note: worried suggests being fretted and shaken up, so the letters are disturbed
about means going around another piece

explanation.surface: A faithful partner is anxious about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: True in the sense of faithful and steadfast towards a person or cause.

clue.text: More pungent in North Africa

definitions.note: a location, standing for the Moroccan city

blocks.note: first meaning: having a sharper, stronger flavour
second meaning: the Moroccan port on the Strait of Gibraltar

explanation.surface: Food tastes stronger in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangy food has a sharp taste, and the comparative names the Moroccan port city.

clue.text: Thatcher's a nonentity

blocks.note: surface reading: an insult to someone who thatches roofs, or to the prime minister
setter's reading: the thing Margaret Thatcher famously declared did not exist

explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher said in a 1987 interview, 'There is no such thing as society', so in her view it is a nonentity, a thing that does not exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher's famous remark denied the existence of the community as a whole, making it a non-thing for her.

clue.text: Where there's no charge for one turn?

explanation.surface: A fairground ride where your first go is free.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram indicator; 'turn' and the question mark hint at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The particle in an atomic nucleus carries no electrical charge, unlike the proton or electron.

clue.text: Writer, a right pain, with little letters on crime

blocks.note: lc means lower case, the small letters

explanation.surface: An author who is an irritating person writes in small letters about a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Carson was the American marine biologist who wrote Silent Spring. 'A right pain' reads as British slang for an annoying person.
explanation.definitionFit: The American biologist was the author of several celebrated books on nature and the sea.
